newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

With weekends away becoming a more popular style of travel for top executives who cannot afford time off from their jobs to travel with their families for a week, Queensland resorts are straining, while boutique hotels a few hours from capital cities are flourishing. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday Australians should not feel they had a racist history, and he criticised teachers who promoted that view. However, while Howard also criticised "ratbags and bigots" on the race issue, he fell short of specifically criticising Independent MP Pauline Hanson for her anti-Asian and anti-Aboriginal views. Page 2.

Bankers Trust-controlled Hamilton Island, which posted a A$54 million loss for the last financial year, has been hit with a Supreme Court writ alleging it has breached the Trade Practices Act by trying to remove a number of lease holders who run business franchises on the island. Page 3.

Metal Trades Industry Association chief executive Bert Evans has warned a new push by metal unions for improved pay and conditions may pose a serious threat to economic recovery and employment prospects in the manufacturing industry. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The lowest wage rises in over two years, coupled with low inflation, has added weight to the call to cut official interest rates. Despite figures showing ordinary full-time earnings rose just 3.5 per cent in the year to August, the Federal Government stil remains divided about the decision to cut rates, with Treasurer Peter Costello refusing to back the stance by Prime Minister John Howard to make such a move. Page 1.

In his most comprehensive discussion on immigration yet, Prime Minister John Howard has predicted the race debate, sparked by outspoken Independent MP Pauline Hanson, would fall by the wayside within three months. Howard declared Australians were not racits or bigots but defended concerns over levels of Asian migration as "legitimate fears". Page 1.

This week's ministerial forum between Indonesia and Australia in Jakarta has led to both countries examining the concept of special economic co-operation zones to link the two nations. The proposal for such zones could eventuate in air and sea links betwen northern Australia and eastern Indonesia. Page 1.

Victorian Solicitor General Douglas Graham, QC, has come under intense pressure to resign following a breach in the State's public sector code of conduct. Graham, who has links with four family companies with BHP shares valued at A$890,000, advised Victoran Attorney-General Jan Wade not to proceed with a contempt action against the mining giant. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Prime Minister John Howard has lashed out at educational authorities for providing the young with incorrect accounts of Australian history, claiming many people had a negative perception of Australia's past. Entering in the immigration and race debate, Howard believed it was destructive to claim the country had a "racist, bigoted past". Page 1.

As William Hegedus opted to stay home from a family outing to study for his Higher School Certificate on Wednesday, he was shot twice in the chest by intruders. The 17-year-old was found bleeding to death at the family house at Inverell in north-west New outh Wales. Police believe Hegedus was shot when he disturbed theives. This latest death follows an outbreak of killings across the State over the past week. Page 1.

A decline in wages growth, coupled with low inflation, has set off intense pressure for an imminent cut in interest rates. An Australian Bureau of Statistics survey showed a rise of 0.7 per cent in average weekly earnings to A$676.70 in the three months to August. This latest figure represents half the rise from the previous quarter. Page 1.

The Police Royal Commission was told yesterday former detective inspector John Wilson denied any knowledge of a plan by police to make token arrests for the 1991 murder of crime figure Roy Thurgar to avoid allegations of a police cover-up. Page 3.
THE AGE

Victorian Attorney-General Jan Wade insisted she was not aware until last week that the State's top solicitor, Douglas Graham, QC, had a major financial interest in BHP. Graham owned BHP shares when he advised the Attorney-General in March not to proceed on a contempt of court prosecution against the company. Page A1.

Police raided the Victoria Racing Club offices last night, seizing documents relating to a controversy involving champion racehorse Encosta de Largo's blood sample readings before the A$175,00 Bill Stutt Stakes at Moonee Valley on 29 September. The investigation comes after the discovery of a one-page handwritten report which noted an illegal bicarbonate reading in the horse. Page A1.

The Department of Foreign Affairs told a Senate inquiry yesterday that a commando-style raid was considered to rescue Australian hostage David Wilson from Khmer Rouge captors in September 1994. However, the plan to save Wilson, who along with two other hstages was executed by the Khmer Rouge, was rejected because of the danger to the hostages. Page A1.

Geelong's City Centre child care manager Joanne Spicer said the mother of Katy Bolger, 3, who died earlier this month in Geelong, showed many signs of being unable to cope. Spicer said she had lost count of the number of times she warned child-protection services about Katy, adding that she had called for help only two days before Katy was found dead. Page A1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
